note: Official test shape 14. The organizer's BaselineTransformer cannot run it: BaselineSelfAttention materializes [B,H,S,S] = 18.6 TB. A speedup against that is undefined, so the comparison is made against the same model with its attention chunked to O(S) memory and nothing else changed -- see `race`, and results/shape14_race_<arch>.json.

measurements.note: Re-measured after the causal tiling default was corrected; this shape relies on that default.

scan.note: How far each GPU gets as S grows, before the two memory fixes were complete; kept because it shows where each limit was.

fixes_required: FlashAttention: attention memory is O(S), not O(S^2), so the 18.6 TB score matrix is never formed.
Batch streaming: no operation in this model mixes batch elements, so the batch is sliced and results written into one output buffer.

SDPA fallback: it would build an [S,S] causal mask (37.25 GiB at S=100000), since SDPA accepts is_causal or an attn_mask but not both. With no padded token the mask is a no-op and is_causal alone is exact: 45.9 GB peak instead of 84.6 GB.

accuracy_at_full_length.method: The reference materializes [B,H,S,S] = 18.6 TB, but the memory is the obstacle, not the arithmetic: chunking query rows and masking against the key index computes the same thing in O(S). The entire output -- all 32 batch elements at the full S -- is gated against that streamed reference, run in fp32 with TF32 disabled (stricter than the organizer's own, which leaves TF32 on) and with a two-pass softmax rather than the online rescaling the kernel uses. Reproduce with `python scripts/shape14.py --gate --batch 32`.

attention_only_sampled_rows.note: A second, narrower check: exact float64 reference on 48 sampled query rows at the full S, attention sub-layer only.

full_stack_where_baseline_fits._note: [fp32 attention, fp16 attention] against the organizer's own baseline

race.method: Two opponents, because the organizer's baseline cannot run this shape. (1) The chunked reference: their own BaselineTransformer with the attention chunked over query rows to O(S) memory and nothing else changed -- entirely our code, and so a weak independence check. Timed first on an unfragmented allocator, chunk size swept, best time taken. (2) The SDPA reference: that same model with the attention replaced by PyTorch's scaled_dot_product_attention, which is not our code and does run this shape. Both under the organizer's own numerics (TF32 on, matmul_precision=high). Reproduce with `python scripts/shape14.py --race`.
race.caveat: `speedup_vs_sdpa` is the figure to prefer: it is against an independently written implementation. `speedup` is against our own chunked reference. Neither is the organizer's unmodified baseline, which cannot run this shape at all. SDPA is also more memory-frugal than we are -- 14.6 GB peak against 30.2 GB -- so the speed is bought partly with memory.
